pr_title: Update the logic to calculate the screen scale on Android
pr_body:
Takes into account the ratio between the screen size and the default window dimensions, which allows to get rid of cropping issues.

Address cropping issue for the Godot Android Editor following https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70863

Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/71198
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/65889
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/71246

[3.x version](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71838)

pr_comments:
> I'm not sure if I understand this logic and how it's related to the min_size

@bruvzg @akien-mga I'll use the pixel 5 screen for reference to provide some context on the issue introduced by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70863 and how this PR resolves it.

The pixel 5 has a screen size of 2340 × 1080 (less is actually available for display because of the system's notification and navigation areas, but it's close enough), and an [extra high pixel density (xhdpi)](https://developer.android.com/training/multiscreen/screendensities#TaskProvideAltBmp) screen.

The extra high pixel density [causes its default scale to be `2`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/cd031fd31a8fdcdae1e93d1b20caf93230f0ac59/platform/android/java/lib/src/org/godotengine/godot/GodotIO.java#L145), so on that device the app has a max effective window size of `1170 x 540`.

[DisplayServer::window_set_min_size(...) is a no-op on Android](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/cd031fd31a8fdcdae1e93d1b20caf93230f0ac59/platform/android/display_server_android.cpp#L394), so prior to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70863, the effective min window size was set by the effective window size of the device, so `540` in this case.
After that PR, the min window size is now properly updated to `600`, which causes cropping at the current scale.

At such, this PR uses the effective window size and the min window size to figure out the largest supported scale to avoid cropping, and then take the minimum between that scale and the scale that matches the device screen density.

> And why display size is hard-coded to 800x600 instead of getting real size from getResources().getDisplayMetrics()

800x600 is the default window size we have for Android (both in 3.x & 4.x), so we're using this as the min window size against the real window size (obtained from the Android view we're rendering to) to calculate the largest supported scale.
Ideally, we'd want to use the dimensions in `DisplayServer::window_set_min_size(...)` but those are set too late (the scale is retrieved before those values are set).

issue_context.title: Android Beta 11 Scaling
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 beta 11

### System information

Android Pixel 4 android 13

### Issue description

Scaling for android beta 11

Beta 10 scaling is fine 
![Screenshot_20230111-214349](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/122491128/211925181-504e7c50-f235-4292-b4a4-cdd6ee74f67e.png)

Beta 11 scaling is off
![Screenshot_20230111-214253](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/122491128/211925334-3d0e03b5-5b77-42e8-a6ae-49cf5d7ab179.png)


### Steps to reproduce

install 

create project 

edit project

### Minimal reproduction project

none needed
comments:
This is not actually a GUI scaling issue, but one of the controls may now be forcing a minimum size that's too high to work on mobile.

If you can [compile the engine from source](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/development/compiling/index.html), you could look into [bisecting the regression](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/community/contributing/bisecting_regressions.html) to greatly speed up troubleshooting.

- 4.0.beta10's commit hash (`good`) is `d0398f62f08ce0cfba80990b21c6af4181f93fe9`.
- 4.0.beta11's commit hash (`bad`) is `91713ced81792b10fdc9367b7f355738e5d52777`.

review_comments: I'm not sure the editor can be used at all in 800x600. And for the project itself the default size seems to be bigger than that (at least for the project setting). Maybe we should bump this one too?

Bumping should be fine, and the default dimensions can be made to match the editor min dimensions: `1024x600`.

Since the application is landscape, the dimension that matters the most is the height. Most Android devices have a 16:9 aspect ratio, so the min height can be updated to `500`. From my testing, the editor UX still fits comfortably within that frame. Lowering the min height also increases the largest supported scale which improves readability.
